precepts.text: Blessed be the Lord my strength, which teacheth my hands to war, and my fingers to fight. David understood the Lord was with him in every fight and battle, and the Lord was teaching him how to fight. David chased a lion and killed it; he fought bears. How was he able to do that? The Lord was with him.
precepts.point: This day will the Lord deliver thee into mine hand; that all the earth may know that there is a God in Israel. And all this assembly shall know that the Lord saveth not with sword and spear: for the battle is the Lord's.

note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

precepts.why:
David said to Goliath, “Thou comest to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a shield: but I come to thee in the name of the Lord of hosts, the God of the armies of Israel”. When we fight and when we war, we war in the name of our God. Then Psalm 144 shows where David's fighting came from: “Blessed be the Lord my strength, which teacheth my hands to war, and my fingers to fight”.

This is David, and he says God is his strength, and it is God that teaches his hands to war. David understood that the Lord was with him in every fight and every battle he was in, and the Lord was the one teaching him how to fight. David didn't go to no kung fu school. The Lord was literally teaching David how to fight. David chased a lion and killed it; David was fighting with bears. How was he able to do that? The Lord was with him.

“and my fingers to fight”: and my fingers to punch a dude and break his teeth. Y'all don't be doing that to nobody today, unless you are defending yourself.

So the Lord is our strength, brothers. Always remember that. That is how you learn to war and fight: the Lord is with you, and you can't war without the Lord warring with you. That is why David could tell the Philistine, “This day will the Lord deliver thee into mine hand”, “that all the earth may know that there is a God in Israel”, and that “the Lord saveth not with sword and spear: for the battle is the Lord’s”. Anytime you go to war, it's the Lord that's with you fighting.

precepts.text: Endure hardness, as a good soldier of Jesus Christ.
precepts.point: Blessed be the Lord my strength, which teacheth my hands to war and my fingers to fight. He handpicked every Israelite to be a soldier.
precepts.why:
“Blessed be the Lord my strength, which teacheth my hands to war, and my fingers to fight.” We serve a God of war, the God that formed the light and created darkness, and that God of war is Christ. David is speaking of how the Lord equipped him with his mighty fighting skills, and the same man of war teaches his soldiers to do the same. Paul says it: “Thou therefore endure hardness, as a good soldier of Jesus Christ. No man that warreth entangleth himself with the affairs of this life; that he may please him who hath chosen him to be a soldier.”

The God of war handpicked every one of us to be soldiers in his mighty army. We are in a boot camp, a training camp, and he is teaching us how to war. Some brothers think they are here just for the unleavened bread, just to be around the brothers. No. Everything going on in the earth, in your household and in the congregation is a teachable moment, because there are spirits in all of it, and we are being built up to deal with those spirits.

It is a process. You start with yourself, subduing your own body, and that is ongoing until you go in the grave. Then your household, then the congregation, as a leader helping other brothers and sisters do the same. Even when you hear somebody else being corrected, it is about you, because at some point you will stand in that same position.

Judges shows why the nations are here: “Now these are the nations which the Lord left, to prove Israel by them”, “to teach them war.” The nations are the Lord's sword to teach us war. If you think that means go get your Glock, you are being simple. “For though we walk in the flesh, we do not war after the flesh.” At Ai the Lord said, “I have given into thy hand the king of Ai”, and still told Joshua, “lay thee an ambush for the city behind it.” The victory is already ordained, but you must go about it the way the Lord commanded. The spiritual side of the war is obedience.

So endure hardness. Some send emails saying, I am no longer with IUIC, I am going to take a break. Taking a break from the Lord? That will not work. A good soldier does not entangle himself with the affairs of this life; he stays in the fight to please the one who chose him.

precepts.text: Our sons as plants grown up in their youth, our daughters as corner stones, polished after the similitude of a palace.
precepts.point: Thy children like olive plants round about thy table. Our children will grow up full-grown in this truth; our sons honored in the age of wisdom, our daughters precious cornerstones, polished daughters of Sarah, eloquent as in the days of old.

precepts.text: Our garners full, affording all manner of store; our sheep bringing forth thousands and ten thousands in our streets.

note.label: Psalm 128: Blessed Is Every One That Feareth the Lord

precepts.why: “That our garners may be full, affording all manner of store: that our sheep may bring forth thousands and ten thousands in our streets”. The wife is that fruitful vine by the sides of the house, the fruit of the womb that is his reward, a fruitful possession producing many children. The blessing fills everything: the garners full, the sheep bringing forth thousands and ten thousands in our streets.

precepts.point: Thy children like olive plants round about thy table. Our children will grow up full-grown in this truth; our sons honored in the age of wisdom, our daughters precious cornerstones, polished daughters of Sarah, eloquent as in the days of old.

note.label: Psalm 128: Blessed Is Every One That Feareth the Lord

precepts.why: “That our oxen may be strong to labour; that there be no breaking in, nor going out; that there be no complaining in our streets.” Our oxen strong to labor, our businesses not taken, and no going out into slavery. That is the house where the wife is a fruitful vine and the children olive plants round about the table.
